Aloevera.uses: Traditionally used in skin-care and herbal preparations. The leaf gel is also commonly used in household and cosmetic preparations.
Aloevera.description: Aloe vera is a succulent plant with thick, fleshy leaves that contain clear gel. It is commonly grown in warm climates and home gardens.

Amla.uses: Amla fruit is widely eaten and used in traditional Ayurvedic preparations. It is also commonly used in food products such as preserves, drinks and powders.
Amla.description: Amla is a small to medium-sized tree that produces round greenish-yellow fruits. The fruit has a sour taste and is widely used in Indian food and traditional practices.

Amruthaballi.uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and herbal practices. Different parts of the plant have been used traditionally in herbal preparations.
Amruthaballi.description: Amruthaballi, also known as Giloy, is a climbing vine with heart-shaped leaves. It commonly grows on trees and other supports in warm regions.

Arali.uses: Traditionally used in Indian herbal practices. The tree also has important cultural and environmental value.
Arali.description: Arali, identified in the dataset as Ficus religiosa, is a large tree with heart-shaped leaves and a long, spreading growth habit. It is commonly associated with South Asian landscapes and cultural settings.

ashoka.uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and herbal practices. The bark and other plant parts have been used in traditional preparations.
ashoka.description: Ashoka is a tropical tree known for its attractive clusters of orange to reddish flowers. It has compound leaves and is commonly grown in warm parts of India.

Astma_weed.uses: The plant has a history of traditional herbal use, particularly in traditional preparations for respiratory complaints. These are traditional uses and should not be treated as a substitute for medical care.
Astma_weed.description: Asthma weed is a small herbaceous plant that commonly grows in tropical and subtropical areas. It has small leaves and inconspicuous flowers.

Balloon_Vine.uses: Traditionally used in various herbal practices. Different parts of the plant have been used in regional traditional preparations.
Balloon_Vine.description: Balloon vine is a climbing plant with delicate leaves and distinctive inflated seed capsules. It grows in warm regions and can spread over nearby vegetation.

Bamboo.uses: Bamboo is widely used for food, construction, crafts and other everyday materials. Some bamboo species also have traditional uses.
Bamboo.description: Bamboo refers to a group of fast-growing grasses with jointed stems. Depending on the species, bamboo can range from small plants to tall woody stems.

Beans.uses: Beans are commonly consumed as food and provide dietary nutrients. Different bean varieties are also used in traditional and regional cuisines.
Beans.description: Bean plants are legumes that produce pods containing edible seeds. They are cultivated widely as food crops.

Betel.uses: Betel leaves are traditionally used in South Asian culinary and cultural practices. They have also been used in regional herbal preparations.
Betel.description: Betel is a climbing vine with glossy, heart-shaped aromatic leaves. It is commonly grown in warm and humid regions.

Bhrami.uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and herbal practices. Brahmi is especially known in traditional preparations associated with memory and general wellness; these are traditional uses, not medical advice.
Bhrami.description: Brahmi is a small creeping herb that usually grows in moist environments. It has small fleshy leaves and spreads along the ground.

Bringaraja.uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and herbal practices, including traditional hair preparations. Leaves and aerial parts have been used in regional herbal formulations.
Bringaraja.description: Bringaraja is a small herb with narrow leaves and small white flower heads. It commonly grows in moist or disturbed areas.

camphor.uses: Traditionally valued for its strong aromatic properties in household and herbal preparations. Camphor products should be used only as directed because concentrated camphor can be harmful if misused.
camphor.description: Camphor tree is an evergreen tree with aromatic leaves and wood. The characteristic camphor compound is obtained from certain parts of the tree.

Caricature.uses: Traditionally used in some regional herbal practices. It is also widely grown as an ornamental plant for its attractive foliage.
Caricature.description: Caricature plant is an ornamental shrub with broad leaves that may have distinctive purple or green patterns. It is commonly grown in tropical gardens.

Castor.uses: Castor seeds are processed to produce castor oil for traditional and commercial uses. Raw castor seeds are poisonous and should never be consumed.
Castor.description: Castor is a fast-growing plant with large palmate leaves and spiny seed capsules. Its seeds contain oil that is processed for several commercial purposes.

Catharanthus.uses: The plant is important in pharmaceutical research because it contains naturally occurring alkaloids. Its compounds have been studied extensively in medicine, but the plant should not be self-used as a treatment.
Catharanthus.description: Catharanthus roseus is a flowering plant commonly known as Madagascar periwinkle. It has glossy leaves and flowers that may be pink, white or purple.

Chilly.uses: Chilli is widely used as food and as a traditional spice. It is commonly included in sauces, pickles, curries and other dishes.
Chilly.description: Chilli is a pepper plant that produces pungent fruits containing capsaicin. The fruits vary widely in size, shape and heat level.

Citron lime (herelikai).uses: Citron is used as food and in traditional culinary practices. Its fragrant rind is also used in preserves, flavoring and regional preparations.
Citron lime (herelikai).description: Citron is a citrus plant known for its large aromatic fruit and thick rind. It is grown in warm climates and is related to other cultivated citrus plants.

Coffee.uses: Coffee seeds are widely processed into a beverage containing naturally occurring caffeine. Coffee is also an important agricultural and commercial crop.
Coffee.description: Coffee is an evergreen shrub or small tree that produces berries containing coffee seeds. The seeds are processed and roasted to make coffee.

Common rue(naagdalli).uses: Rue has a history of traditional herbal use. Because concentrated preparations can be unsafe, it should not be used medicinally without appropriate expert guidance.
Common rue(naagdalli).description: Common rue is an aromatic perennial herb with blue-green leaves and small yellow flowers. It has a strong characteristic smell.

Coriender.uses: Coriander is widely used as a culinary herb and spice. It also has a long history of use in traditional food and herbal practices.
Coriender.description: Coriander is an aromatic annual herb with delicate leaves and small flowers. Both its leaves and dried seeds are commonly used in cooking.

Curry.uses: Curry leaves are widely used in Indian cooking and traditional herbal practices. Fresh leaves are commonly added to curries, chutneys and tempering.
Curry.description: The curry leaf plant is a small tree with aromatic pinnate leaves. Its leaves are widely recognized as an important ingredient in South Indian cooking.

Doddpathre.uses: Traditionally used as an aromatic culinary herb and in regional herbal preparations. The leaves are also valued for their strong fragrance.
Doddpathre.description: Doddpathre is an aromatic succulent herb with thick, soft leaves. It is commonly grown around homes in warm regions.

Drumstick.uses: Moringa leaves and pods are widely consumed as food and have traditional uses. The plant is also valued as a nutrient-rich food crop.
Drumstick.description: Drumstick, or moringa, is a fast-growing tree with compound leaves and long slender pods. Its leaves, flowers and pods are commonly used as food.

Ekka.uses: Calotropis has a history of traditional use in some regional practices. Some plant parts and latex can be toxic, so medicinal use requires expert guidance.
Ekka.description: Ekka is a flowering shrub with large leaves and distinctive waxy flowers. It produces milky latex when its tissues are damaged.

Eucalyptus.uses: Eucalyptus is traditionally used for its aromatic properties. Leaves and essential oils are used in some household and herbal products, but concentrated oils require careful handling.
Eucalyptus.description: Eucalyptus is an evergreen tree known for its strongly aromatic leaves. Many species grow rapidly and are cultivated in warm and temperate regions.

Ganigale.uses: Ganigale has a history of traditional use in regional practices. Some plant parts and latex can be toxic, so it should not be used medicinally without expert guidance.
Ganigale.description: Ganigale is a tropical flowering shrub identified in the supplied data as Calotropis gigantea. It has broad leaves and produces milky latex.

Ganike.uses: The plant has a history of traditional use in some herbal systems. Some parts may be toxic depending on the plant stage and preparation, so medicinal use requires expert guidance.
Ganike.description: Ganike is a small herbaceous plant with small flowers and dark berries. It commonly grows in fields, gardens and disturbed areas.

Gasagase.uses: Poppy seeds are used in cooking and traditional food preparations. Other parts of the plant contain regulated alkaloids and should not be used as home remedies.
Gasagase.description: Gasagase is identified in the supplied data as a poppy plant with flowers and seed capsules. Poppy seeds are commonly used as a food ingredient.

Ginger.uses: Ginger is widely used as a spice and has a long history of traditional use. It is commonly added to food, tea and other preparations.
Ginger.description: Ginger is a perennial herb whose underground rhizome is widely used. The rhizome has a strong aroma and a warm, spicy taste.

Globe Amarnath.uses: Traditionally used in some herbal practices and widely grown as an ornamental plant. The dried flower heads are also used in decorative arrangements.
Globe Amarnath.description: Globe amaranth is a flowering plant recognized by its rounded flower heads, which may be purple, pink or white. It is commonly grown as an ornamental plant.

Guava.uses: Guava fruit is widely consumed as food, while leaves have traditional uses. The fruit is commonly eaten fresh or used in juices, jams and other foods.
Guava.description: Guava is a tropical fruit tree with oval leaves, pale flowers and edible fruits. The fruit usually has a fragrant aroma and may contain many small seeds.

Henna.uses: Henna leaves are traditionally used as a natural dye for skin, hair and textiles. Henna is also important in cultural and decorative practices.
Henna.description: Henna is a flowering shrub whose leaves contain natural coloring compounds. It grows well in hot, dry climates.

Hibiscus.uses: Hibiscus has traditional uses in several cultures and is also widely grown as an ornamental plant. Flowers and leaves are used in some traditional food and herbal preparations.
Hibiscus.description: Hibiscus is a flowering shrub with large colorful flowers and glossy leaves. It is widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical gardens.

Honge.uses: Honge has traditional uses and is valued for its seeds and oil. The oil is also studied and used for non-food applications such as biofuel and other products.
Honge.description: Honge is a tropical tree with compound leaves and clusters of flowers. Its seeds contain oil and the tree is valued for several practical uses.

Insulin.uses: Traditionally used in some herbal practices. Claims about blood-sugar effects should not be treated as established medical treatment, and medical conditions require professional care.
Insulin.description: The insulin plant is a tropical perennial with broad leaves and upright stems. It is commonly grown as an ornamental and herbal plant.

Jackfruit.uses: Jackfruit is widely consumed as food, and its seeds are also eaten after cooking. Different plant parts have additional traditional uses in some regions.
Jackfruit.description: Jackfruit is a large tropical tree that produces very large fruits directly from the trunk and branches. The fruit contains sweet edible sections surrounding seeds.

Jasmine.uses: Jasmine flowers are widely used for fragrance, garlands and traditional cultural practices. Some species are also used in regional herbal preparations.
Jasmine.description: Jasmine refers to flowering plants known for their highly fragrant flowers. Many jasmine species are grown in warm climates as garden and ornamental plants.

kamakasturi.uses: Basil is widely used as a culinary herb and has traditional herbal uses. The leaves are commonly used fresh or dried for flavor and aroma.
kamakasturi.description: Kamakasturi is an aromatic basil-type herb with fragrant leaves. It is commonly grown in warm climates and used as a culinary or herbal plant.

Kohlrabi.uses: Kohlrabi is primarily consumed as a vegetable. The swollen stem is commonly eaten raw or cooked in different dishes.
Kohlrabi.description: Kohlrabi is a vegetable crop with a swollen edible stem that grows above the soil. It also produces leafy greens that can be eaten.

Lantana.uses: Lantana has a history of traditional use in some regions, but parts of the plant can be toxic. It should not be used medicinally without expert guidance.
Lantana.description: Lantana camara is a flowering shrub with clusters of small colorful flowers. It grows readily in warm regions and can spread aggressively.

Lemon.uses: Lemon is widely used as food, flavoring and in traditional household practices. Juice and zest are commonly used in drinks, cooking and preserves.
Lemon.description: Lemon is a citrus tree producing aromatic yellow fruits with acidic juice. The tree has glossy leaves and fragrant white flowers.

Lemongrass.uses: Lemongrass is widely used as a culinary herb and aromatic plant. It is commonly used in teas, soups, curries and other foods.
Lemongrass.description: Lemongrass is a grass with long narrow leaves and a strong lemon-like aroma. It forms dense clumps and grows well in warm climates.

Malabar_Nut.uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and herbal practices. The leaves have a history of use in traditional herbal preparations.
Malabar_Nut.description: Malabar nut is a shrub with elongated leaves and distinctive flowers. It is commonly found in warm parts of South Asia.

Malabar_Spinach.uses: Malabar spinach is commonly consumed as a leafy vegetable. The leaves and young stems are used in soups, curries and other dishes.
Malabar_Spinach.description: Malabar spinach is a climbing plant with thick, fleshy green leaves and soft stems. Despite its name, it is botanically different from common spinach.

Mango.uses: Mango fruit is widely consumed as food, while different plant parts have traditional uses. Raw and ripe mangoes are used in many Indian dishes and preparations.
Mango.description: Mango is a large evergreen tree producing the well-known mango fruit. Its long leaves and dense canopy are characteristic of the species.

Marigold.uses: Marigold is widely cultivated as an ornamental plant and has traditional uses. Flowers are also used in garlands, decorations and some traditional preparations.
Marigold.description: Marigold is a flowering plant recognized by its bright yellow or orange flower heads. It is commonly grown in gardens and cultivated for decorative purposes.

Mint.uses: Mint is widely used as a culinary herb and aromatic plant. Fresh or dried leaves are commonly added to drinks, chutneys, salads and other foods.
Mint.description: Mint is a group of aromatic plants with strongly scented leaves and square stems. It grows readily in moist soil and is widely cultivated.

Neem.uses: Neem has a long history of traditional use in Ayurvedic and herbal practices. Different plant parts are used in traditional preparations and household applications.
Neem.description: Neem is a tropical evergreen tree commonly found throughout South Asia. It has compound leaves, small white flowers and bitter fruits.

Nelavembu.uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and other herbal practices. Its bitter aerial parts are used in some traditional herbal preparations.
Nelavembu.description: Nelavembu is a small herbaceous plant with narrow leaves and an upright branching stem. It is commonly found in warm regions.

Nerale.uses: The fruit is widely consumed and different plant parts have traditional uses. The ripe fruit is commonly eaten fresh or used in drinks and preserves.
Nerale.description: Nerale, or Indian blackberry, is a tropical evergreen tree producing dark purple fruits. The fruits have a deep color and a sweet-to-astringent taste.

Nooni.uses: Noni has a long history of traditional herbal use in several regions. Traditional use does not establish that it can treat a medical condition.
Nooni.description: Noni is a tropical plant producing a distinctive pale fruit with a strong odor when ripe. It has broad green leaves and grows well in warm climates.

Onion.uses: Onion is widely consumed as food and has traditional culinary uses. It is used in a wide range of dishes, pickles and sauces.
Onion.description: Onion is a bulb-forming plant widely cultivated as a vegetable. It has hollow green leaves and a strong aroma when the bulb is cut.

Padri.uses: The supplied data describes Padri as having regional traditional uses. Specific medicinal claims should be verified against a reliable botanical or medicinal source before use.
Padri.description: Padri is a tree species included in the medicinal-leaf dataset. It is a woody plant with leaves characteristic of its tree growth habit.

Palak(Spinach).uses: Spinach is widely consumed as a leafy vegetable. It is commonly cooked in curries, soups and other dishes.
Palak(Spinach).description: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable with soft green leaves and a short growing cycle. It is commonly cultivated in home gardens and farms.

Papaya.uses: Papaya fruit is widely consumed as food and different plant parts have traditional uses. Ripe fruit is commonly eaten fresh, while unripe fruit is used in cooking.
Papaya.description: Papaya is a tropical plant with large leaves and soft edible fruit. The plant can grow quickly in warm climates and produces fruit throughout suitable seasons.

Parijatha.uses: Traditionally used in Indian herbal practices. The flowers and other plant parts have also been used in regional cultural and traditional preparations.
Parijatha.description: Parijatha is a flowering tree known for its fragrant white flowers that open at night. Its flowers have orange centers and are commonly collected for cultural use.

Pea.uses: Peas are widely consumed as food and provide dietary nutrients. Fresh or dried peas are used in many regional dishes.
Pea.description: Pea is a leguminous plant producing edible pods and seeds. It is commonly grown as a cool-season vegetable crop.

Pepper.uses: Black pepper is widely used as a spice and has traditional culinary uses. It is commonly added to curries, soups, spice blends and beverages.
Pepper.description: Black pepper is a climbing vine producing clusters of small pepper berries. The berries turn dark after processing and drying.

Pomoegranate.uses: Pomegranate fruit is widely consumed as food and has traditional uses. The arils and juice are commonly used fresh or in food preparations.
Pomoegranate.description: Pomegranate is a shrub or small tree producing round fruits filled with edible arils. The fruit has a tough outer skin and juicy seeds.

Pumpkin.uses: Pumpkin is widely consumed as food and its seeds are also used as food. The flesh is commonly cooked in curries, soups and other dishes.
Pumpkin.description: Pumpkin is a creeping or climbing plant with large leaves and large fruits. The fruit can vary in shape, size and color depending on the variety.

Raddish.uses: Radish is widely consumed as a vegetable. The roots are commonly eaten raw, cooked, pickled or added to curries and salads.
Raddish.description: Radish is a fast-growing root vegetable with leafy foliage and edible roots. Root color and shape vary among cultivated varieties.

Rose.uses: Rose is widely cultivated for flowers and fragrance and has traditional applications. Rose petals are also used in some foods, drinks and cosmetic preparations.
Rose.description: Rose refers to flowering plants known for their fragrant and colorful flowers. Many rose varieties are grown in gardens for ornamental and cultural purposes.

Sampige.uses: Traditionally valued for its fragrant flowers and cultural uses. Flowers are used in garlands, worship and fragrance-related preparations.
Sampige.description: Sampige is a flowering tree known for its strongly fragrant yellow-orange flowers. It grows well in warm climates and is valued for its fragrance.

Sapota.uses: Sapota fruit is widely consumed as food. It is commonly eaten fresh or used in shakes, desserts and other food preparations.
Sapota.description: Sapota is a tropical evergreen tree producing sweet brown fruits. The fruits have soft brown flesh and a characteristic caramel-like flavor.

Seethapala.uses: The fruit is consumed as food and the plant has traditional uses. Ripe fruit is commonly eaten fresh or used in drinks and desserts.
Seethapala.description: Seethapala, or custard apple, is a tropical fruit tree producing sweet segmented fruits. The tree has broad leaves and a rounded canopy.

Spinach1.description: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable with soft green leaves and a short growing cycle. This dataset class represents a spinach variety or duplicate class label.

Tamarind.uses: Tamarind is widely used as food, seasoning and in traditional preparations. The sour pulp is commonly used in curries, chutneys, drinks and sauces.
Tamarind.description: Tamarind is a large tropical tree producing brown pods containing sour edible pulp. Its compound leaves are small and delicate.

Taro.uses: Taro is widely consumed as a cooked food crop. The leaves and corms are used in different regional cuisines after appropriate preparation.
Taro.description: Taro is a tropical plant with large heart-shaped leaves and edible underground corms. The corms must be properly cooked before eating.

Tecoma.uses: Traditionally used in some herbal practices and widely grown as an ornamental plant. Specific medicinal use should be verified before use.
Tecoma.description: Tecoma is a flowering shrub or small tree with bright yellow flowers. It is commonly grown as an ornamental plant in warm regions.

Thumbe.uses: Traditionally used in various Indian herbal practices. Different parts of the plant have been used in regional traditional preparations.
Thumbe.description: Thumbe is a small herbaceous plant with white flowers arranged around its stems. It commonly grows in open areas and warm regions.

Tomato.uses: Tomato is widely consumed as food and is an important culinary crop. The fruit is used fresh, cooked, dried and in sauces.
Tomato.description: Tomato is a cultivated plant producing edible red, orange or yellow fruits. It is widely grown in gardens and farms.

Tulsi.uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and herbal practices. The leaves are also commonly used in traditional drinks and household preparations.
Tulsi.description: Tulsi is an aromatic plant widely grown in India. It has fragrant leaves and small flowers and is commonly cultivated around homes and temples.

Turmeric.uses: Turmeric rhizomes are widely used as a spice and in traditional preparations. Turmeric is a common ingredient in Indian cooking and food products.
Turmeric.description: Turmeric is a perennial herb whose underground rhizome has a distinctive yellow-orange color. The rhizome is dried or used fresh in cooking.
